title: Credit-reserving tier router with regional affinity & soft fallbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a tier-aware routing layer that reserves small per-tenant credit windows and prefers regional capacity. The router should: 1) allocate a short-term reservation token for incoming requests from free/paid/enterprise plans to avoid head-of-line starvation; 2) prefer local region replicas for latency-sensitive routes but allow soft spillback to other regions when reservation would otherwise block requests; 3) support graceful fallback to cheaper/quantized model variants when quota is exhausted or regional capacity constrained; 4) expose metrics that attribute preemption/demotion events to tenant and plan for billing and SRE analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Router honors reserved credit window per tenant and does not drop in-flight requests while reservation valid
Regional affinity policy routes >=85% of P99-latency requests to same-region pools under normal load
Soft fallback triggers automatically when reservation and regional options are exhausted and selects compatible model variant
End-to-end e2e tests cover free/paid/enterprise admission, reservation expiry, cross-region spillback, and model-variant fallback
Monitoring dashboard shows reservation utilization, preemptions, and per-plan fallback rates
implementation_notes: Admission: add lightweight reservation token store (in-memory + Redis fallback) that grants 100-300ms reservation windows keyed by tenant and route
Decisioning: compute score = weight(plan) * local_capacity_factor - age_penalty; use score threshold to accept/demote/spillback
Fallbacks: maintain compatibility matrix between model variants (e.g., llama-2-13b->quant-13b, or gpt-3.5-lite) to ensure response semantics remain acceptable
Telemetry: tag requests with admission_reason (reserved|direct|spillback|fallback) and surface in Console for cost/latency analysis
Safety: circuit-breaker per-plan to avoid cascade on cross-region spillbacks; incorporate cooldown windows
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Initial design RFC posted to Confluence with proposed reservation token API and scoring function. Feedback requested from runtime and SRE teams.

2025-02-18: Implementation spike completed for in-memory reservation store. Microbench shows <200ns median token allocation under contention. Spike notes pushed to Drive: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/spikes/ENG-21777-reservation-spike
2025-02-24: Prototype integrated into canary router; observed 10% improvement in free-plan tail latency during controlled burst tests. Logged issues on spillback oscillation under rapid load changes.

2025-03-01: Design updated to add cooldown and jitter to spillback decisions based on SRE feedback. Added compatibility matrix for fallbacks and a small PR to runtime for model variant tagging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123
2025-03-04: Began e2e test authoring; front-end flag gating planned for console visibility in next iteration
review_feedback: SRE (Marco Rivera): prefer Redis-based durable reservations only for enterprise plans; free/paid can use in-memory with eventual consistency. Also recommended adding per-region capacity soft limits to avoid lateral hotspots.
Product (Nina Summers): add guardrail to avoid downgrading enterprise models unless explicit override; product concerned about quality regressions for high-paying customers.
Design (Priya Malhotra): suggested exposing a visual indicator in Console that shows when requests were served from fallback models to help debugging and billing conversations.
Security (Omar Khalid): no KMS changes required but asked to include audit events for reservation grants and fallback triggers
notes_and_tradeoffs: Reservation window size trades off between latency protection and utilization. Chose conservative 200ms default after load testing; configurable per-plan.
Cross-region spillback improves availability but increases p99 if remote links are slow. Mitigated by preferring model variants with faster decode profiles when spilling back.
Durable reservations for enterprise improve fairness under failure but add Redis cost and complexity; hybrid approach reduces ops surface.
Fallback model variance: we accept small semantic drift for free/paid plans but require model fidelity thresholds for enterprise to avoid SLA violations
